nodes.natural_language: If a>0 then the quadratic ax^{2}+bx opens upwards and is nonnegative outside the interval with endpoints 0 and -b/a; the presence of the negative root -b/a therefore forces D to contain an interval of negative numbers, contradicting D\subseteq[0,\infty).
nodes.statement: a>0 implies D contains negative numbers, contradicting tc_3.

nodes.natural_language: The range of f is contained in [0,∞), so if the domain D equals the range then necessarily D\subseteq[0,∞).
The inequality x(ax+b)\ge0 together with D\subseteq[0,∞) forces D to be a closed interval of the form [0,c] or [c,∞) (or a singleton) for some c\ge0.
nodes.statement: D = {x \in ℝ | a x^{2} + b x \ge 0} \subseteq [0,∞) implies D is [0,c], [c,∞) or {0} for some c \ge 0.
